## 8. If he becomes the fall guy: the "owners slept" defense

If Salvador breaks on cross, or his papers turn against him, expect Atty. Ramos to let the de la Fuentes take the fault and argue that the loss falls on the owners who let them act (red-team directive, §3A). The order of the cross protects against this.

1. **Lock S11 and S13 first.** Get "my father showed Mrs. Balane the SPA" and "that is the SPA of 16 March 1992" before any question that hurts him. Once he is under pressure he may minimize. Those two answers defeat apparent authority (Art. 1911): a buyer shown the real power, with its class and consultation limits, did not rely on an appearance of broader power.

2. **Then the anomalies (Part 7).** They show the agent's side exceeded the power. Under Art. 1898 that makes the sale void unless the owners ratify. Their blaming the agent concedes the excess.

3. **Ratification needs knowledge.** No paper shows any heir knew of the Balane sale before 2020 or received a peso of it. His tax papers end in November 1998, and he gave no accounting when asked in writing (CORR-007).

4. **Remedy.** Art. 1897 gives the buyer a claim against an agent who exceeds his powers. Arts. 1891 and 1892 make the agent's side account to the owners. Neither reaches the owners' land.

**The law on inaction (statutes only; read any case on lawphil before citing it).** There is no prescription against the registered owner (PD 1529 §47). The action on a void contract does not prescribe (Art. 1410). Art. 1911 makes the principal liable; it does not convey land. Revocation protects only against those with notice (Arts. 1921 to 1922); that is why the case leads with the class limit and keeps revocation in the alternative.

**The honest gap.** From 2005 to 2020 nothing in the record shows the owners told any occupant of the revocation, annotated it, or demanded an accounting. The 2019 statement shows the heirs' remaining land in arrears. Do not argue diligence for those years. Argue three things: the buyer saw the real limits (S11, S13); the limits were on the title from 1996 (PD 1529 §52); and the Balane side knew of the dispute before registration. From 2020 onward the owners acted on the record: publication in 2020, then the adverse claim annotated on Gloria's own title in May 2023. That is two years and nine months before suit, which answers "slept" for the period that matters to laches.
